qid.description: <agent>-<YYYYMMDD>-<NNN>, shared by every artifact of one question (4.5.5)

thread.description: solo-<qid> when no bridge round is involved (5.2)

grade.description: Evidence grade (5.3). E6 may not appear in any card; the validator rejects it.

source.description: Where the number came from. The grade is derived from this prefix, never self-reported (check 21). operator_read is a value the operator read off the instrument; operator_recall is one they stated from memory, and the two do not deserve the same grade. prior_run is something another project ran and recorded -- reference it as <project>@<sha> -- and it is E3 because 10.3 rule 1 says a run taken elsewhere is not a run taken here: there is no run_id from this system and that day's calibration state cannot be reproduced. literature is a published claim that is not a vendor specification; spec covers the vendor and left the textbook and the paper with no prefix to be. Neither addition changes what grade anything gets -- both were already E3 by rule. They exist so a fact can state its kind instead of borrowing a wrong one or carrying none, which check 43 counts as self-reported. A number the operator CHOSE rather than observed -- a target, a tolerance, a budget -- does not belong here at all. It carries neither source nor grade, the way a ceiling in envelope/safety.json does (5.3, ruled 2026-09-19). An operator_set prefix was added for one and reverted: SOURCE_GRADE is a function from source to grade and P2 derives one from the other, so a decision either yields a grade it should not have or leaves a hole in the invariant. The line is not between numbers that feel like targets and numbers that do not -- it runs between the person's goal and everything computed from it, and what is computed keeps its source and grade. A solidus is allowed in the token as of 2026-09-19: every bandpass filter is designated centre/width -- FF01-595/31-32 -- so excluding it excluded the canonical form of a whole class of part, and the librarian seat had to write spec:FF01-595-31-32 with the true designation in identifiers.part_number. That is reversible and the identifier is where an exact designation belongs anyway, but a source token that does not match the part it names reads fine until somebody greps for it.

precision.description: order_of_magnitude means at most one significant figure is claimed (5.8, P15)

number.description: A value only means something with its unit, its source and its grade (P2).

at.description:
WHERE this value is a reading of, when that is not the whole of what the entry or card is about. A registry id where one exists -- a device or configuration -- so it can be resolved rather than read, or the reserved word `ambient` for the room. Optional, and absent means the value refers to its subject without qualification.

It sits on the number and not on the entry because the two split inside one entry: trapping_laser_identity carries `wavelength 1064 nm`, which has no place, and `rated_max_power 5 W`, which is at the generator and false everywhere the beam actually goes.

Matching does NOT read this, and cannot. `validity` is a map from quantity to interval, so it can say where a quantity is BOUNDED and not what a value is a READING OF; the two are different claims and the second had nowhere to go. Two entries hit it on 2026-09-19 -- 5 W at the generator, and 20 C that is the room's and not the sample's -- and both fail the same quiet way, by being applied at a point they were never measured at. One is a curiosity; two is this field.

`ambient` is a reserved word and not a registry, decided 2026-09-19. The question raised was whether a locus needs a registry of places; the answer came from counting. Every `at` that resolves points at a driven channel, and the only locus that has ever failed to is the room -- one item. A registry of one is not a registry, and a place registry with no membership rule would become what kb_entry's own description calls `quantity` before today: a de facto registry rather than a declared one. The test that settled it is in plan.md 4.6: does this registry have a reason to exist other than resolving a subject? Quantities passed it and got contracts/quantities.json; samples passed it and get a table beside the device table; places did not, and get this word. If a second non-device locus ever appears, that is the day to revisit.

formula.description: required when source is computed:. Arithmetic over other number names in this card.

inputs.description: required when source is computed:. Names this formula reads.

derived.description: This computed value is a NAMED quantity: it carries a `symbol`, and one symbol means one definition across every card and the store (check 36). **It does not mean dimensionless.** A census on 2026-09-18 found 6 uses, all six carrying a unit (five `s`, one `N*s/m`), against 20 numbers with the dimensionless unit `1`, none of them derived — zero overlap. The documented meaning had never once been used, and six authors had independently read it as written here. Uses a computed: source; not a separate source kind.

symbol.description: The name this quantity goes by, e.g. `k_star` or `tau_d`. Dimensionless or not: what a symbol buys is that one name means one definition (check 36), and two definitions that also differ in dimension break a comparison more quietly, not less.

origin.description: for synthesis cards: <file>#<name> the value was carried from (check 12)

allOf.$comment: derived and symbol require each other: a named quantity is one that is named. Deliberately NOT tied to `formula` -- 18 numbers compute from a formula without being named quantities (diffusivity, exposure_time_chosen, box_length_min_dilution), and requiring the flag of them would fail correct work in three boundaries at once.

assumption.description: Every assumed: number must be explained here (check 4).

falsifier.description: what observation would retire this assumption

gap_ref.description: gap_id in kb_gaps: the librarian was asked and could not supply it (check 39). Required when the card reached the librarian at all; degraded says when it did not.

authorised_by.description: <person>_<yyyymmdd>, when a person directed that a value be carried past the range its source covers -- a curve's endpoint used for a wavelength beyond it, a spec read at one condition applied at another. It does NOT change the grade: being told to use a value is not evidence for it, and the moment an authorisation could lift E5 to E3 the grade scale becomes a permission scale and stops measuring anything. What it buys is the E5/E6 boundary. Once an extrapolation is written down as a number it looks identical whether a person directed it or a model invented it, and E5 may enter a card while E6 may enter nothing; without this field an auditor cannot tell them apart. A model may never fill it -- that would be a laundering path from E6 into a card. It belongs on the assumption and never on a KB entry: the entry says what is true at the condition its source covers, and who stretched it is a property of the plan that stretched it.

kb_ref.description: What the librarian returned, and the grade it returned it with (4.3.1).

kb_gap.description: What the librarian was asked for and could not supply (4.3.1). kb_refs records what came back; without this, what did not come back is recorded nowhere and the discovery of a gap dies with the server.

gap_id.description: what an assumption's gap_ref points at

kind.description: five kinds because the next action differs for each: search / find other conditions / ask a person / do not enter it / read it from your own snapshot (4.3.1). The fifth was added 2026-09-19 after the service's first real use answered `absent` to device_registry, control_channel and read_back -- a table name and two of its column names, all three sitting in the caller's own snapshot under tables.devices, published by the librarian and pinned by sha256. `absent` is not merely unhelpful there: its next action is search-outside-then-ask-a-person, so it sends the caller out of the building for what it already holds.

published_in.description: Which published table holds it. Required when kind is in_published_table, because two of the three names that found this defect were COLUMN names -- a caller told only that it is 'in a table' guesses which. Carrying the sha256 is what makes the next action checkable rather than advisory: read tables.<table> and confirm it is the version the store published.

snapshot.description: the kb/exports/snapshot_<agent>.json it was published into

column.description: set when the caller asked for a column rather than the table

searched.description: where it was looked for. A gap with nothing here is not a gap: not-looked-for and not-there are different claims.

nearest.description: entries that came close, so that 'nothing like it exists' and 'it exists at another temperature' stay distinguishable

overlap.description:
How the near-miss entry stood against the query, and each word carries its own subject.

`partial` -- the intervals intersect and the query is not fully covered; the uncovered part is named.
`disjoint` -- the quantities WERE compared and their intervals do not intersect at all. Added 2026-09-19 because the verdict line was `full if not uncovered else partial`, with no branch for disjointness, so eight refractive-index entries pinned to single wavelengths came back `partial` against a query at 605 nm that intersects none of them. `partial` is an invitation to clip to the nearest edge, which is exactly the judgement 4.3.1 keeps on the caller's side. match() already computed the truth -- it writes `uncovered.<q>.disjoint: true` into the same row -- and the verdict a caller reads disagreed with it. Leaving it in `uncovered` alone would have repeated 21c5325, where conflict_with was computed correctly and left out of the projection anyone reads.
`no_overlap` -- the entry constrains no quantity the query mentioned, so there was nothing to compare. This is about the SETS of quantities; `disjoint` is about the intervals. Task 004 separated those two meanings out of one word once, and reusing `no_overlap` here would have recollided them.

`unconstrained` was this enum's name for `no_overlap` until 2026-09-18 and was kept while cards migrated. **Removed 2026-09-19, the contract step**: no card on disk carries it, verified before dropping it. The row-level `overlap` a caller sees in `entries[]` also has `full` and `unstated`; neither can reach here, because `nearest` holds only entries that were compared and fell short.

near_names.description: Names the store DOES answer to that are close to what was asked. Required by check 49 when kind is `absent`, and an empty array is a real answer -- it says the neighbourhood was searched and nothing was near. The key being absent says the search never ran, and then the gap may only claim 'not found under this name', not 'it does not exist'. Separate from `nearest` because the two search different axes: `nearest` holds entries that answered to the NAME and fell short on CONDITIONS, so `absent` -- emitted exactly when nothing answers to the name -- can never carry one. The two were structurally unable to back each other. Added 2026-09-19 after the service's first day: of nine empty kb_query answers, eight were the store holding the knowledge under another word or in a published table, and only one was honestly not there. `numerical_aperture` returned absent while six entries held it as `na`. Suggesting is not matching: a name here returns nothing and asks the caller to ask again, so it cannot make a wrong string answer as though it were right -- which is why folding whitespace into the matcher was refused while this is not the same move.

asked_by.description: the caller_id the fan-out executor issued (4.3.1)

then.$comment: Conditionally required rather than advised. The alternative rejected for this kind -- put the next action in `nearest` and leave `kind` alone -- failed because nothing branches on a field nobody has to fill. A gap that says only in_published_table repeats that mistake one level down: it names the shelf and not the book, and the caller who asked for a column guesses.

criterion.description: Machine-readable stop/success criterion, declared before execution (5.4). A stop criterion also declares what being met means (on_met); a success criterion does not need to, because a success criterion being met is what success is.

number.description: name of the threshold in numbers[]. Exactly one of number and target: a threshold is either a claim about the world, graded and sourced, or a decision (5.3.1).

window.description: optional: over what interval the metric is evaluated

on_met.description: What it means for this criterion to be met. Without it `met: true` is not comparable between cards: result.json records sc_drift as met with outcome DONE, where met says the guard held, while a simulation's step_displacement_diverged is met exactly when the run broke. Same field, opposite meaning, and outcome is derived from it. continue: the condition still holds and the run proceeds; the stop is the violation. complete: the run has reached its planned end. fault: something broke and the run stops short of that end.

target.description: metric of the threshold in targets[], when the threshold is a decision rather than a number. Added 2026-09-19: a success criterion compared against the accuracy target, and when the target left numbers[] the criterion had nothing to point at. Check 6 resolves either, so the guarantee moves to the new container rather than being dropped.

criterion.$comment: `number` left `required` on 2026-09-19 when `target` became its alternative: the threshold is still mandatory, and which of the two carries it is the oneOf below. Dropping it from `required` without that oneOf would have made a criterion with no threshold at all writable.

interval.description: An allowed range on one parameter. min or max may be absent (one-sided).

basis.description: what this bound rests on: a name in numbers[], or `kb:<entry_id>` for a bound that rests on a served entry rather than a computed number. The second form was added on 2026-09-19 (5.3.2) because A4's numbers[] is empty and its bounds stand on kb_refs -- all 28 intervals then in the repository named numbers[] entries, so a bound grounded only in the store could not be written at all. It reuses the `kb:` prefix 5.3 already defines rather than minting a second name for the same thing. **This reference resolves**: the entry_id must appear in that card's kb_refs, and a check can say so -- unlike the declaration-reading checks, nothing here is taken on trust.

condition_bound.description: One quantity's interval in canonical physical units (D7). min or max may be absent (one-sided), but not both.

condition_range.description: A map from quantity name to interval (4.3.1). Both sides of a condition query use this shape -- a query's condition_range and an entry's validity -- because one has to be compared against the other, and prose cannot be compared. That is why validity_conditions stays separate and human.

kb_gaps.description: the other side of kb_refs: asked for and not supplied. Not empty is normal (4.3). Every assumed: number points at one of these unless degraded says the librarian was never reached (check 39).

contrast.description: What a sample provides and a configuration requires. One list, two readers: a goal's sample_contrast and a capability's requires_contrast. Declared once because two parsers of one vocabulary drift, and the one that drifts says something false without erroring (0.4-6).

caller_id.description: Who is asking, and the server's isolation unit (4.3.1). Four forms: <qid>:v<N>:s2, <qid>:v<N>:<config>:<axis>, <qid>:v<N>:operator, and bridge:<thread>:r<N>. The bridge hangs off a thread and a round rather than a question, because one thread crosses two qids -- one per side -- and the bridge: prefix lets a parser split the id without knowing the namespace. The revision is part of it because without it a re-run's a1 shares a session context with the attempt it exists to replace; revision 1 writes v1 rather than omitting it. The axis form without v<N> is still accepted while the cards that predate a6dca6a migrate, and stops being accepted after. Declared in 4.3.1 and repeated nowhere: while this pattern held the axis form alone, s2, operator and bridge: were declared and the server refused them, and a refused call leaves no line in queries/log.jsonl -- so the only visible symptom was a seat that stayed degraded. The bridge branch is as tight as the two fields it is built from: the thread is a `thr-` thread, because that is what `thread` allows and a `solo-` one has no round in it, and the round starts at 1, because round 0 means no bridge round is involved. A looser branch would let a query be logged under a thread that cannot exist or a round that cannot, and the log is the only evidence a query happened -- a line no round can ever be matched to is the attribution missing while the line looks fine. A fifth form, `selftest:<what-is-being-tested>`, is reserved for verification traffic. It collides with no qid and no thread, so a reader can tell a line a test produced from a line a round produced -- the log does not record the calling process, so without separate namespaces there is no way to tell. It is not an exception to the rule that an id is issued rather than chosen: a selftest impersonates no round, so there is nothing to issue.

target.$comment: A target is a DECISION and carries no source and no grade -- the same reason a ceiling in envelope/safety.json carries none (5.3.1). A grade says how far a claim can be trusted; a decision is correct by being made. Inline rather than by reference into numbers[], so a grade is not merely absent but inexpressible: an opt-in guard is not a chokepoint (2.1 rule 9). Defined once here because goal, plan and result all carry it -- three copies of one shape is what 11-11 counts. A carried copy is compared against the goal's by check 52; it is pinned rather than referenced for the reason kb_version is pinned, that a plan_approval fixes the plan and not the goal, so a pin that resolves to whatever the goal says now is not a pin.

allowed_set.description: A discrete set of permitted values on one parameter, where an interval cannot say it. Two axes need it and they need different value types: A4's selector exclusivity is a set of strings, and A6's magnification is a set of numbers because the turret and the 1.5x zoom make it discrete (4.5.3). It is not an interval: intervals require a unit, and a unit means nothing for a selector name. Like an interval it **intersects**, so S4 combines it with ranges and with other sets the way it already combines ranges.

values.description: the permitted values, all of one kind

unit.description: required when the values are numeric, meaningless when they are not

excluded.description: values ruled out, named rather than left implicit, when saying what is forbidden carries more than saying what remains

basis.description: what this bound rests on: a name in numbers[], or `kb:<entry_id>` for a bound that rests on a served entry rather than a computed number. The second form was added on 2026-09-19 (5.3.2) because A4's numbers[] is empty and its bounds stand on kb_refs -- all 28 intervals then in the repository named numbers[] entries, so a bound grounded only in the store could not be written at all. It reuses the `kb:` prefix 5.3 already defines rather than minting a second name for the same thing. **This reference resolves**: the entry_id must appear in that card's kb_refs, and a check can say so -- unlike the declaration-reading checks, nothing here is taken on trust.

precondition.description: A constraint that restricts no value and instead requires something of the plan. A4's selector verifiability is the case: no selector on this configuration can be read back, 2.1 makes an unverified state non-proceedable, and the conclusion is that the loaded state must be established by acquisition. **It does not intersect, it propagates** -- if any axis returns one, the plan must carry it. That is why it is not an allowed_set: S4 intersects sets, and a precondition folded into one would be silently dropped the first time an intersection was taken.

requires.description: what the plan must do, as an instruction and not a description

basis.description: what this bound rests on: a name in numbers[], or `kb:<entry_id>` for a bound that rests on a served entry rather than a computed number. The second form was added on 2026-09-19 (5.3.2) because A4's numbers[] is empty and its bounds stand on kb_refs -- all 28 intervals then in the repository named numbers[] entries, so a bound grounded only in the store could not be written at all. It reuses the `kb:` prefix 5.3 already defines rather than minting a second name for the same thing. **This reference resolves**: the entry_id must appear in that card's kb_refs, and a check can say so -- unlike the declaration-reading checks, nothing here is taken on trust.
